CMMC stands for Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification.
It is the Department of Defense (DoD)'s mechanism for validating that defense contractors implement required cybersecurity practices, including those from NIST/800-171.
NIST/800-171 defines security requirements for protecting Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) in nonfederal systems.
CMMC is the certification and assessment framework used to verify conformance to those requirements for relevant DoD contracts.
The Cloud Native Computing Foundation is the Linux Foundation foundation that hosts vendor-neutral open-source infrastructure projects, starting with K8s, which seeded it in 2015.
It holds each project's trademarks and pays for shared infrastructure, so no single vendor controls a project's direction. It also runs KubeCon + CloudNativeCon.
Each project sits at one of three levels, set by votes of the Technical Oversight Committee (TOC), per the project lifecycle:
Sandbox — early-stage projects the foundation is willing to host.
Each project sits at one of three levels, set by votes of the Technical Oversight Committee (TOC), per the project lifecycle:
Incubating — projects with real production users and a healthy group of maintainers.
Each project sits at one of three levels, set by votes of the Technical Oversight Committee (TOC), per the project lifecycle:
Graduated — mature, widely adopted projects that have passed a security audit and a governance review.
Each project sits at one of three levels, set by votes of the Technical Oversight Committee (TOC), per the project lifecycle:
K8s — container orchestration. Graduated in 2018, the first project to do so.
OpenTelemetry — vendor-neutral traces, metrics and logs. Graduated on 2026-05-21 (announcement).
OpenFeature — vendor-neutral feature flag API. Incubating since 2023-11-21.
Lima — Linux VMs on macOS, the base of Colima. Incubating since 2025-10-14 (announcement).
Podman — daemonless container tools, with Podman Desktop. Sandbox since 2025-01-21 (project page).
The full catalog is the CNCF Landscape.
CNMAT (Center for New Music and Audio Technologies) is a multidisciplinary research center at Uni/California/Berkeley focused on the intersection of music, technology, and performance.

As a pioneering institution, CNMAT addresses the evolving needs of composers, performers, and technologists by developing innovative tools and frameworks that enable new forms of musical expression and real-time interaction.
Interdisciplinary integration – combining music, computer science, engineering, and acoustics.
Real-time performance – emphasizing low-latency, expressive musical control.
Open tools and standards – building reusable, extensible systems for the global community.
